proposal:
# Re-rank proposal 11 (D148, loop boundary after card 208): lock the process into the template as soon as the record-order fix lands

- Led by: the product manager seat (fresh context, pm-rerank-11). Claude seat because probes at 23:03 UTC show Codex, Copilot, Grok and agy without usable quota (.mob/records/probes/2026-10-30.jsonl).
- Trigger: loop boundary after card 208 (the fresh-probe seat gate with least-recently-used rotation). Its work, review, gate, sign-off and retro (D165) are done; its schema-1 record is held, like card 209's, because card 214 closed first (.mob/records/blockers/2026-10-30-209-record-order.md, updated). Card 208 therefore leaves the order; it is not re-ranked.
- Before (note 10): 208, 219, 210, 211, 220, 221, 222, 223, 224, 225, 217, 218, 213, 216, 212, 215, 206, 207.
- After: the record-order fix (219), the record checker hardening (210), the MD-010 fix (211), the default templates carrying the pending process rulings (216), the loop's corrective-card gate (220), the loop running a card in its own repository (221), the loop's steps that stop on failure (222), the per-card retro from every role (223), the re-rank by the product manager and a Decider (224), card mode reading only role lines (225), the acceptance-suite flakes (217), the mid-card retro removal (218), then 213, 212, 215, 206, 207.
- Next card: the record-order fix (219). It is waived from the stop-the-line gate by the product owner (D162), and when it is on main it releases two held records (cards 208 and 209).
- Rationale (one line): the record-order fix (219) starts first because it frees the two held records, and the default templates card (216) moves up from after the acceptance-suite flakes (217), the mid-card retro removal (218) and card 213 to right after the record checker hardening (210) and the MD-010 fix (211), because product owner direction D161 says lock the process into tooling and the template first, and it is a thin docs-and-template slice with no dependency that 212 and 215 build on.
- Reversal stated: move the default templates card (216) back behind the loop's corrective-card gate (220) if the facilitator gate refuses its start while findings block, since the order must not promise what the gate will not honour.

## What changed and why
- Card 208 leaves the list: nothing is left to do except its record, which lands with the record-order fix (219). 219 moves from second to first, with no other card ahead of it.
- 210 and 211 keep their order. The record checker hardening (210) edits the same checker as 219 and binds hand-run cards today; the MD-010 fix (211) is records only.
- 216 moves up from position 13 to position 4 (nine places). Reasons: D161 puts the template with tooling as the first thing to lock; the card has no dependency, only documentation and templates change, and it enables 212 and 215 (their runner and record parts then enforce text the template already states). The loop cards 220 to 225 keep their order behind it, so no tooling card is delayed by more than one thin slice. 217, 218 and 213 each move down by one place or more only because 216 passes them; their relative order is unchanged.
- 212 and 215 keep their relative order and now follow 216 with only 213 between.

## The feedback-loop lens (D165): joins card 216, no new card
The card 208 retro decided that the feedback-loop lens (the nested loops from the input of the retro: for each loop, who or what gives the feedback, how fast it arrives, and what the team does with it) becomes a standing section of the retro, and that a card puts it into the mob-defaults template. Card 216 is that card, and the lens joins its scope as a card-text change at 216's ready step, decided by objection window (D153), not as a separate card:
- It is the same file and the same kind of change as 216's addition 2: 216 already states "the stand-down replaced by the full retro at Done" in TEAM_WORKING_AGREEMENT.default.md, and the lens is one more standing section of that retro. A separate card would edit the same template section, and would add a second red template test for the same text and a second review and audit, with a conflict risk between the two.
- It stays thin. The lens is a lens, not a mandate and not an experiment (D165 C5), so it needs no hypothesis, metric or counter-metric; it adds one section to the template and one test.
- The card text needs these edits at ready, and only these: (a) the Source line says seven additions, adding "(7) the feedback-loop lens as a standing retro section (D165)"; (b) Done check 1 gains the lens, so it stays at three checks (the card allows at most three): the retro section is stated with the per-loop questions and cites D165, with a red template test first; (c) the Observes line adds the lens; (d) "Not in this card" no longer says "new rulings beyond the six" but "beyond the seven", and still excludes the intent-restatement experiment from D165, which is a trial of the avowry team and is not a template default until its trial retro decides keep.
- Reversal for this part: if any polled role at 216's ready window objects that the lens makes the card too large for D136, split the lens into its own card ranked directly after 216, with no change to the order above.

## Evidence considered
- Re-rank note 10 (.mob/records/reranks/2026-10-30-10.md): the current order and the product owner waiver of the record-order fix (D162).
- Blocker .mob/records/blockers/2026-10-30-209-record-order.md: cards 208 and 209 records held; both land after 219 is on main.
- D165 votes (.mob/records/deciders/D165-votes.json) and the retro input (.mob/records/208/retro-proposal-nested-loops.md): the lens as a standing retro section, put into the template through a card (D161).
- Card 216 text (gh issue view 216): Contract, no dependency, three Done checks, six additions, enables 212 and 215, docs and templates only.
- Probes at 23:03 UTC: only Claude usable.
- Not checked: the current open findings in the audit ledger, so whether the facilitator gate lets a non-corrective card start now is for the delivery lead to confirm in the window.

## Neither a one-way door nor a standing-rule change
The Rank field is edited in git and can be reversed by the next re-rank. It changes no agreement, D-record, checker or published claim. The card-text change to 216 is a separate card-text window, as was done for 212 and 215 at note 5.

## Window rule: every declared role polled (F-054)
Every declared role is polled in this window: architect, QA engineer, backend developer, independent reviewer (audit lens), delivery lead, and product manager (signoff). The product manager (ready) is the proposer and is not polled. The facilitator, the Decider and the external auditor are never seats and are not polled as roles. An empty or silent reply is re-polled and recorded as an attempt, not counted as no objection.
